## Three Desk Failures {.center}

A forecast that was **too confident**.

. . .

A portfolio that looked **diversified** — and wasn't.

. . .

A model declared **fair** — that wasn't.

. . .

All three are the *same* mistake about one thing: **dependence**.

## One Noun, Three Verbs {.center}

This course turns on a single idea — **dependence** — and the three things you
ever do with it:

. . .

**measure** it   ·   **remove** the part you may not keep   ·   **propagate** it
honestly

. . .

…and one operation underneath all three: a **change of variables**.

## The Axiom {.center}

> **Claim only what your evidence justifies.**

. . .

The least-committal distribution for what you know is the most honest one — and
the **Gaussian** is the least-committal joint of all.

. . .

So *what we add to or remove from a Gaussian is exactly the dependence in the
data.*

## The Through-Line

| Module | Verb | Question |
|---|---|---|
| 1 · Dependence | **measure** | how much do two things move together? |
| 2 · Gaussianization | (the engine) | turn messy data Gaussian, invertibly |
| 3 · Uncertainty | **propagate** | carry risk forward without losing the tail |
| 4 · Fair learning | **remove** | make a model blind to a chosen variable |

. . .

The same change-of-variables map runs **forward** to measure and remove,
**backward** to propagate.

## How the Course Runs {.center}

- Concepts on slides — ELI5, no ML background assumed (calculus + basic
  probability is enough).
- Then a **hands-on demo** per module, on real S&P 500 data.
- Every figure here is generated by code in the repo and reproducible live.

. . .

Let's start by learning to **[measure dependence](01-dependence.qmd)**.
